transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in because... I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. It’s just awful. I mean, I work in personal care, helping out folks in their homes, and the nurses and the families I work with—oh, speaking of the nurses, they completely changed the shift schedule at the agency last week and it has been a total mess. I had to drive all the way across town during rush hour on Tuesday just to cover for someone who called out sick. The traffic on the interstate was just unbelievable, completely backed up for miles because of some fender bender. 

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right, my face. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just feel like it’s the very first thing everyone notices when they look at me. The families I work for, the nurses, even the people at my church. Actually, at the church potluck last Sunday—Pastor Miller’s wife made her famous potato salad, she uses that sweet relish in it which I just love—I couldn't even enjoy myself or look people in the eye because I just know they're all staring right at my neck.
How much time do you spend thinking about this sagging or uneven spot on your jaw and neck each day?

Oh, gosh, how much time? I... I don't really know. I've never actually timed it or kept track of the hours or anything like that. I just know it's on my mind a lot when I'm getting ready in the bathroom. 

Actually, speaking of the bathroom, the light fixture over my sink has been flickering since Wednesday. It’s one of those long fluorescent tubes, you know? And it makes this awful buzzing noise. I asked my landlord to send someone to fix it, and the guy he sent—Gary, I think his name was—he tracked mud all over my good bath mat. I had to throw it right in the wash with a bunch of bleach. It's a real shame too, because it was this lovely peach color I got on clearance at Target, and they don't even make that shade anymore, so if the stain doesn't come out, I don't know what I'll do. 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right, the time. Yeah, I couldn't give you an exact number, I'm just really not sure.
Can you estimate how much of your day is taken up thinking about the sagging or uneven spot on your jaw and neck?

I really wish I could give you a better estimate, doctor. I just... I don't know how to put a number on it. It just feels like it's always there, humming in the background, you know? Kind of like that refrigerator I had in my old apartment on 4th Street. Oh, that place was a nightmare. The fridge would just hum and rattle all day and night. I complained to the property manager—this woman named Brenda who always wore these huge, clunky earrings—and she told me I was just being sensitive. Sensitive! Can you believe that? I mean, I was paying good money for that place, and the least they could do is make sure the appliances work without sounding like a lawnmower in the kitchen. I ended up having to buy my own earplugs just to get a wink of sleep. 

But anyway... yeah, I just don't have a good guess for how many hours or anything. I'm sorry, I just don't know.
Do you find yourself checking your appearance in mirrors or other reflective surfaces because of concerns about your jaw or neck?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. Before I leave for work or... or any kind of meeting, really, I just keep going back into the bathroom. I'll stand at the mirror and try to fix my collar, you know, pull it up a bit, or adjust my hair so it falls right around my neck to cover it. And then I'll pull out my phone and use the camera to take another look, just to be sure. 

Actually, speaking of my phone, I just had to get a new one because my old one—it was a Samsung, I think—the battery just completely died on me. I took it to that kiosk in the mall, the one right next to the Auntie Anne's pretzels, and the young man working there told me it would cost more to replace the battery than to just buy a new phone! Can you imagine? And the smell of those pretzels while I was waiting was just overwhelming, all that butter and cinnamon sugar. I used to get them all the time when my daughter was little and we'd go back-to-school shopping. 

Oh, my daughter... yes, sometimes I even ask her if my neck looks strange before I leave the house. She gets so frustrated with me, bless her heart. I've actually been late to work more than once because I just can't stop checking and adjusting everything. It's just... it's exhausting, honestly.
Does this concern about your jaw and neck ever interfere with your work, relationships, or other important parts of your life?

Well, yes, it definitely does. At work, I've actually passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on the supervisory pieces, just because I worry people will be staring right at my face and my neck the whole time. And I've fallen behind on my paperwork, too, because I get so stuck in the morning trying to make myself look presentable that I end up rushing the rest of the day. 

I work at the salon down on Elm Street, you know, and we just got this new line of hair products in. They're supposed to be all organic, infused with argan oil and rosemary, but honestly, the smell is just so strong. It reminds me of my grandmother's house when she used to make those herbal sachets for her drawers. She had this big oak dresser, beautiful piece of furniture, but one of the handles was always loose. My grandfather promised to fix it for years, but he was always out tinkering with his old Chevy truck in the garage. He loved that truck more than anything, I swear. 

Oh, right, my life outside of work... yeah, it affects that too. I've actually stopped going to some of my book club meetings and my walking club activities. Just the thought of getting ready and worrying about how my neck looks... it just feels like too much effort, so I stay home instead.
